Product: A manufactured good or offered service available for sale. Also called good, item, merchandise, ware. Examples: a pair of shoes, a car rental, a TV episode.
ProductGroup: A template grouping product variants that differ only in size, colour, or material. Also called product family, product line, variant group.
ProductModel: A specific model or vendor specification of a product. Also called model, product version, datasheet.
SomeProducts: An indefinite set of similar products of the same kind. Also called bulk products, assorted products.
Vehicle: A machine for transporting people or goods, such as a car, motorcycle, or bus. Also called conveyance, automobile, motor vehicle.
Car: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle for passenger transport. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto.
BusOrCoach: A large road vehicle carrying many passengers; a coach is a long-distance luxury bus. Also called bus, coach, omnibus.
Motorcycle: A two-wheeled motor vehicle. Also called motorbike, bike.
MotorizedBicycle: A bicycle with an attached motor to assist or power it. Also called moped, e-bike, motor-assisted bicycle.
Drug: A chemical or biological substance used as medical therapy. Also called medicine, medication, pharmaceutical. Examples: aspirin, insulin.
DietarySupplement: An ingestible product supplementing the diet with vitamins, minerals, or other nutrients. Also called supplement, nutritional supplement. Examples: vitamin D tablets.
BioChemEntity: Any biological, chemical, or biochemical thing, such as a protein, gene, or chemical. Also called biochemical entity, biomolecule.
ChemicalSubstance: A portion of matter of constant chemical composition. Also called chemical, compound, substance. Examples: water, glucose.
MolecularEntity: A distinct atom, molecule, ion, or radical identifiable as a separate entity. Also called molecule, chemical entity.
Gene: A unit of inheritance in DNA affecting biological traits. Also called genetic locus, hereditary unit. Examples: FOXP2, BRCA1.
Protein: An amino-acid-based biological molecule. Also called polypeptide, protein molecule. Examples: amyloid-beta, haemoglobin.
